title: Revenue Concentration — Cumulative % Per Customer
description:
Show each customer's revenue and cumulative revenue percentage (sorted highest to lowest) to illustrate the Pareto 80/20 principle.

**Table: customer_revenue** — `customer_id`, `name`, `revenue`

Output columns: `name`, `revenue`, `cumulative_pct`. Order by `revenue` DESC.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE customer_revenue (customer_id INT, name VARCHAR, revenue INT); INSERT INTO customer_revenue VALUES (1,'Alice',45000),(2,'Bob',38000),(3,'Carol',12000),(4,'Dave',8000),(5,'Eve',5000),(6,'Frank',3000),(7,'Grace',2000),(8,'Henry',1000);
solution_sql: SELECT name, revenue, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY revenue DESC) / SUM(revenue) OVER (), 2) AS cumulative_pct FROM customer_revenue ORDER BY revenue DESC

test_cases.description: 8 customers; Alice and Bob together represent ~71% of revenue; top 3 exceed 80%; last row cumulative_pct = 100.00

hints: SUM(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY revenue DESC) computes a running total in descending order; divide by the grand total for the percentage.
The last row in the result will always have cumulative_pct = 100.00 since it includes all revenue.
explanation: Total revenue = 114000. Alice: 45000/114000 = 39.47%. Alice+Bob: 83000/114000 = 72.81%. Top 3 (add Carol): 95000/114000 = 83.33% — already over 80% of revenue is concentrated in 3 of 8 customers (37.5%), demonstrating the Pareto principle. The cumulative_pct reaches 100% at the last row.
